body.value:
1. this statement, and they said [ …
  2. a man in a craft that does not resemble \\it//, and he does not need other people. We …
  3. among them this statement. But it has become difficult for the servants in it to put forward (?).
  4. We are now dragged off to the sugarworks (al-sukkar, or possibly a variant on 'forced labor,' sukhra) and beaten with sticks, and told: "Come, do
  5. the government's work." We used to bear the hardship in … Jews (?)
  6. for us, and we would say: "We will carry some of our burdens for you." But now we no longer have the strength
  7. to hold out in this situation. Rather, our aituation is disordered and we have gone on our faces (i.e., humbled ourselves before you).
  8. We have turned to God, may His mention be exalted, and to your exalted excellency so that you will speak to
  9. the chief of police (ṣāḥib al‑shurṭa) and the official in charge of these matters about [ … ] of this, and inform him
  10. that the Jews have barred us from this work, and have put under a ban ([a]ḥ[r]amū, i.e. a ḥerem) anyone
  11. of us who does this work. Among us is [one who …] leaving the [ … ], and one who works as a runner (raqqāṣ, a government agent), and who will not
  12. go back to this work. So may your exalted excellency do for his servants what
  13. brings him closer to God, and win the reward (from God) owed for us, and our prayers. May God answer
  14. the righteous prayers his servants offer for him. If he does this, he will be acting graciously and generously.
  15. I have informed him of this [ … ] be gracious, and may his welfare increase forever.
